The underlying send step answers with a forbidden response, but the listing fallback misreads that response on a path ending in a slash as a directory without an index file and serves the listing anyway. An unauthenticated client can enumerate the names of files and subdirectories, recursively, inside dot-directories the operator explicitly denied, such as version control, backup, and key file names. File contents remain protected and only names are disclosed. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.12, and users should upgrade to 10.1.12 or later. As a workaround, disable directory listing or do not serve a root that contains dot-directories.

t: NLTK incomplete fix: additional JVM/JAR sandbox bypass through unvalidated launcher tokens in java() command arguments
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: AllowlistUnpickler does not deny numpy submodule-local file-I/O sinks
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, allowlisted_pickle_load keys dangerous NumPy globals by export name, allowing submodule-local numpy.lib file input/output callables to evade the denylist under the broad module allowance used by TransitionParser. A crafted pickle can invoke recfromtxt to read a local file or open_memmap to create or truncate an attacker-selected file when a victim loads an untrusted model. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: @fastify/static vulnerable to route guard bypass via default index and extension resolution
d: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

t: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in Tree.fromlist causes denial of service via deeply nested list input
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Tree.fromlist recursively converts nested Python list input into Tree objects without enforcing a maximum tree depth. An attacker-controlled list nested beyond the interpreter recursion limit can raise RecursionError and terminate the current parse operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signatures in libdigidocpp
d: Improper certificate validation vulnerability in Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) libdigidocpp, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc4, and Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on Android and iOS. This issue affects libdigidocpp: from 3.13.0 before 4.5.2; DigiDoc4: from 4.0.0 before 4.11.2; DigiDoc: from 3.0.0 before 3.2.0.

t: NLTK: XMLCorpusView comment and CDATA parsing permits quadratic CPU denial of service
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in semantic-logic type parser causes denial of service via nested type strings
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the semantic-logic read_type parser recursively processes both halves of nested complex type strings without applying LogicParser.MAX_PARSE_DEPTH. An attacker-controlled type string or signature with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through Type.fromstring or type-checking entry points and abort the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in WordNet Synset hypernym walkers (max_depth/min_depth/hypernym_paths/hypernym_distances) causes DoS
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.max_depth, min_depth, hypernym_paths, and hypernym_distances recursively follow attacker-controlled corpus pointers without a visited-node set or depth cap. A cyclic or excessively deep hypernym graph can raise RecursionError and terminate traversal APIs and similarity operations that depend on them. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK): Uncontrolled recursion (crash DoS) in DependencyGraph.tree()/triples()
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, DependencyGraph.tree and DependencyGraph.triples walk parsed dependency edges through unbounded Python recursion and do not use a working cycle or depth guard. A crafted CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency file containing a sufficiently long chain can raise RecursionError when the documented traversal APIs are called, aborting the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: Downloader cyclic collection indices cause an infinite closure walk
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6.7 until 3.10.4, nltk.downloader follows collection membership without tracking already visited collection nodes. A self-referencing or mutually referencing collection index can therefore make the package-closure walk loop indefinitely while its queue and memory usage grow, denying service when a victim processes the attacker-influenced index. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in DependencyGraph traversal causes denial of service via deep dependency chains
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. In 3.10.3 and earlier, DependencyGraph._tree and triples recurse once per dependency edge without a depth bound, and get_cycle_path also lacks a visited-set termination guard. A deeply chained or cyclic attacker-controlled CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency structure can raise RecursionError and abort a parse worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: Compile-time regex DoS in NLTK search/tokenizer sinks: quadratic regex-engine compile bypasses the match-only timeout
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: NLTK: StreamBackedCorpusView constructor os.stat leaks out-of-root file existence, size, and mtime bypassing pathsec ENFORCE
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, StreamBackedCorpusView performs os.stat on a caller-supplied plain string path during construction before pathsec containment is enforced. The PathPointer branch used by in-tree corpus readers is validated, so exploitation requires application code to pass an attacker-influenced string directly to the public constructor. That string can identify an out-of-root path and disclose its existence, size, and modification time even though opening the file would be rejected. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Missing authentication for critical function leading to reflected cross-site scripting in JTL-Shop
d: The preview mode of the OPC (OnPage Composer) page builder of JTL-Shop is activated by a request parameter alone and renders page data supplied in the request without checking for an authenticated backend session with the corresponding permission. Several portlet properties are output without output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a visitor or administrator who opens a crafted link; in the case of an administrator, actions can be performed with the administrator's privileges. Third-party plugins whose portlets evaluate property values as templates can additionally be made to execute template code through the same entry point. This is a separate flaw in such plugins and does not affect the portlets of JTL-Shop itself.

t: NLTK: Quadratic-time DoS in SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline on an unterminated corpus line via per-iteration full-buffer rescan
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline appends each new block to a growing character buffer and reruns splitlines over the entire buffer on every iteration. An attacker-controlled corpus file containing one very long unterminated line therefore causes quadratic CPU consumption in line-oriented corpus readers and can deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in example data generation and BreezingForms import in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in example data generation and BreezingForms import in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Example data generation and the BreezingForms import did not check the core.create permission for the affected forms, allowing backend users to create records without permission.

t: NLTK: ARFF_Formatter Injects Weka ARFF Schema Directives via Attacker-Controlled Class Labels
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.classify.weka.ARFF_Formatter writes attacker-controlled class labels into the Weka ARFF @ATTRIBUTE '-label-' declaration without safely formatting the label tokens. Crafted labels can alter the generated ARFF schema or records, corrupting classifier input and causing integrity loss or processing failure. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing access check in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing access check in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The public reload task did not check form and field access levels, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve results of SQL field statements of restricted forms.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - SQL injection in backend data search and export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - SQL injection in backend data search and export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Search filters and form IDs in the backend data view and export were not properly sanitized, allowing SQL injection by backend users.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Improper per-form authorization for field management in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Improper per-form authorization for field management in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Field creation, editing and ordering checked permissions against a user-supplied form ID instead of the form the field belongs to, allowing backend users to manage fields of other forms.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Predictable and reusable email verification codes in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Predictable and reusable email verification codes in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Email verification codes were derived from the email address, did not expire after use and could be guessed without attempt limits, allowing bypass of the email verification.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Stored XSS via SQL field labels in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Stored XSS via SQL field labels in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Labels and values of SQL field options were returned unescaped by the reload task and inserted into the page as HTML, allowing stored XSS if the statement reads user-supplied data.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing authorization and CSRF checks in reset and check-in tasks in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing authorization and CSRF checks in reset and check-in tasks in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The tasks to reset submitted data and to check in forms lacked authorization checks and CSRF protection.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in form creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in form creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The createForm task of the form creator did not check the core.create permission, allowing backend users without create permission to create forms.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Verification mail rate limit reset in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Verification mail rate limit reset in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The rate limit for verification mails was reset on every form render, rendering the limit ineffective.

t: NLTK: Untrusted search path in prover9/mace4 config allows local code execution via relative binary_location
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Prover9Parent.config_prover9 and Mace accept a relative binary_location and pass it to find_binary as path_to_bin, disabling the bare-name absolute-path guard. A local attacker who can plant prover9 or mace4 in the resolved working directory can cause subprocess.Popen to execute that binary with the invoking user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Stored cross-site scripting in JTL-Shop
d: The visitor tracking of JTL-Shop automatically registers unknown crawler user agents without filtering the value, and the stored value is rendered without output encoding on several pages of the administration backend (search engine statistics, crawler dashboard widget, crawler edit form, sitemap export download list and campaign details). An unauthenticated remote attacker can store script code with a single request. The code is executed in the browser session of an administrator who opens one of these pages, allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Authorization bypass in saveAjaxTextarea task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Authorization bypass in saveAjaxTextarea task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The saveAjaxTextarea task did not check edit permissions and accepted arbitrary table and column names, allowing backend users to modify the configuration of any form, including notification recipients.

t: NLTK: Quadratic CPU exhaustion in NLTK XMLCorpusView.read_block via deeply nested XML corpus tags
d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, XMLCorpusView.read_block rebuilds the full root-to-node context path with "/".join(context) for every start tag while searching for a matching element. Deeply nested attacker-influenced corpus XML therefore causes quadratic pure-Python work and can pin a processing worker, resulting in denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated SQL injection in frontend data view filters in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated SQL injection in frontend data view filters in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Sorting, location radius and published filters of the frontend data view were not properly sanitized, allowing SQL injection, partly without authentication.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing SQL statement permission check in form import and field creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing SQL statement permission check in form import and field creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The core.create.sql.statement permission was not enforced when importing forms or creating new fields, allowing backend users without this permission to store arbitrary SQL statements.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated verification mail amplification in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated verification mail amplification in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The verification mail task accepted arbitrary form IDs and recipients without rate limiting, allowing unauthenticated attackers to trigger mass verification mails and database entries.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Access restriction bypass for form submissions in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Access restriction bypass for form submissions in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Form submissions did not check the access level of the form, allowing guests to submit forms restricted to specific user groups.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Path traversal in file upload in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Path traversal in file upload in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - File names of uploads were not reduced to their base name when the option to retain original file names was enabled, potentially allowing files to be written outside the upload directory.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Arbitrary file write leading to remote code execution in CSS editor in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Arbitrary file write leading to remote code execution in CSS editor in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The CSS editor did not restrict file names, extensions and paths of created and saved files, allowing privileged backend users to write arbitrary PHP files.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Arbitrary file deletion via path traversal in CSS editor in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Arbitrary file deletion via path traversal in CSS editor in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The delete and rename tasks of the CSS editor lacked authorization checks, CSRF protection and path validation, allowing backend users to delete files outside the CSS directory.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Open redirect on invalid form submission in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Open redirect on invalid form submission in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The return parameter of an invalid form submission was not validated, allowing redirects to external sites.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Code injection via calculation formulas in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Code injection via calculation formulas in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Calculation field formulas were executed using PHP eval() without validating their content, allowing backend users with field edit permissions to execute arbitrary PHP code.

t: Jupyter MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding can hijack the Jupyter backend through management routes
d: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the same browser-origin controls to the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding so that its hostname resolves to a loopback, LAN, VPN, or published-container MCP listener, then send a browser-shaped request that /api/connect accepts to replace runtime_url and document_url values and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure. The attacker can thereby cause Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to reach that infrastructure and can use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. The default broad bind can increase exposure, but the vulnerability is the missing management-route origin boundary, not a lack of Host validation on /mcp. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated SQL injection in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated SQL injection in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Input placeholders in SQL field statements were inserted without quoting in the public reload task, allowing unauthenticated SQL injection in read queries.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - IDOR in backend data export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - IDOR in backend data export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The backend export did not correctly verify permissions for the exported form, allowing backend users to export data of forms they are not authorized to access.

t: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Open redirects in data view controller and after form submission in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1
d: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Open redirects in data view controller and after form submission in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Return and redirect URLs taken from user input in the data/PDF controller and after a successful form submission were not validated, allowing redirects to external sites.

t: Jupyter MCP Server: Unauthenticated management routes can hijack the Jupyter backend in standalone HTTP mode
d: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode can enforce MCP_TOKEN on /mcp while leaving the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes unauthenticated. An unauthenticated network caller can use /api/connect to replace runtime_url and document_url values and their tokens, reset ServerContext, and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure, causing the server to send Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to that backend. The caller can also use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. This boundary failure does not require explicit insecure no-auth mode and occurs outside normal MCP JSON-RPC tool dispatch. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

t: Stored cross-site scripting in JTL-Shop
d: When the setting for saving requests to non-existent pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in its redirect table, and the administration backend renders it without output encoding in the form used to edit a redirect. An unauthenticated remote attacker can store script code with a single request, which is executed in the browser session of an administrator who opens the affected redirect, allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges. The setting is disabled by default in new installations but may still be enabled in older ones.

t: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git configurations
d: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for embedded line-ending control characters. A malicious repository can insert control characters such as line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

t: Git LFS may leak HTTP headers after redirections
d: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one for which the header was intended. That unintended host can therefore receive cookies containing credentials or other confidential values. Authorization headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts and are not the affected secret in this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

In ConnectWise Automate versions prior to 2026.11, a condition in Web Control Center (WCC2) authorization handling could allow an authenticated contact user to access information associated with other clients on the same Automate server through API requests. This may result in disclosure of information outside the user’s assigned access scope. The issue is limited to information disclosure and does not extend existing modification or command execution permissions. This issue is resolved in ConnectWise Automate 2026.11.

t: Quarkus-vertx-utils: quarkus-vertx-utils: denial of service via worker thread exhaustion on client disconnect
d: A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils. When a client disconnects while receiving a streaming response, the server fails to detect the closed connection and continues processing the data indefinitely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by repeatedly initiating streaming requests and disconnecting, exhausting worker threads and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

t: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git LFS configurations
d: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

t: Gimp: gimp: uninitialized stack disclosure in xcf tile loader
d: A flaw was found in GIMP. Opening a crafted XCF with a truncated uncompressed tile can expose uninitialized main-process stack memory through the imported layer's pixel data, which may include process addresses that weaken ASLR.

t: Openstack-cinder: storwize: cinder: ssh command injection through incomplete metacharacter validation in storage drivers
d: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

t: Git LFS may attempt arbitrary remote commands via crafted SSH URLs
d: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH URL path component as a single argument when constructing remote object-transfer or authentication commands. Shell metacharacters in the SSH URL can therefore escape the intended path argument and cause arbitrary command execution when the remote Git LFS service passes received commands to a shell without adequate sanitization. Git LFS also incorrectly encodes default HTTPS URLs when an SSH URL is configured and the remote host either does not support Git LFS remote commands over SSH or supports HTTP authentication over SSH but git-lfs-authenticate does not return an explicit HTTP URL. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

t: falcon-rust: Discrete-Gaussian sampler runs at 2^-33 precision, far below Falcon's requirement (reference KAT vectors no longer pass)
d: falcon-rust is a Rust implementation of the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme. Prior to 0.2.0, the discrete-Gaussian sampler in src/samplerz.rs evaluates approx_exp, ber_exp, and sampler_z acceptance probabilities with FixedPoint64 values having only 32 fractional bits. The scaling in approx_exp quantizes its input and limits relative precision to about 2^-33, below Falcon's required bound, causing reference known-answer vectors to diverge and invalidating the proof assumption that secret-dependent signature and key distributions are negligibly close to the ideal discrete Gaussian. This is a cryptographic-soundness defect and no practical key-recovery attack has been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.2.0.

t: django-docutils unsafe Docutils defaults allow local file disclosure, SSRF, and stored XSS
d: django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

t: Sprout Track: Authentication bypass via default JWT signing secret
d: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application. Prior to 1.3.5, Sprout Track uses a publicly known hardcoded signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset, and standard setup does not generate a unique secret. On a network-reachable affected deployment, an unauthenticated attacker can sign JWTs with arbitrary claims, including system-administrator claims, to access administrative functionality and read or modify family, child activity, account, and email data. Deployments with a strong unique JWT_SECRET are not affected. Managed and hosted instances were reported remediated. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.5.

t: Frappe: Comment Spoofing via add_comment
d: Frappe is a full-stack web application framework. Prior to 15.108.0 and 16.18.3, the add_comment handler in frappe/templates/includes/comments/comments.py trusts the client-provided comment_by and comment_email fields. A caller can submit chosen identity metadata that is stored with a comment, causing the comment to appear to originate from another name or email address. This issue is fixed in versions 15.108.0 and 16.18.3.

t: sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 Credential Leak via Cross-Host HTTP Redirects
d: sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

t: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 Stack Buffer Overflow via aacs_resolve_path()
d: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against the wrong buffer. Local attackers can place a symlink with a long target on a disc path a user opens to overflow resolved_path[] and link[], crashing the process or potentially executing code if mitigations are bypassed.

t: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via PNG Decoder Filters
d: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Reconstruct in src/Bitmap.c that occurs when AVERAGE and PAETH filters process zero-width PNG images. A malicious multiplayer server can supply a crafted texture pack URL or player skin to write past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing connecting clients.

t: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via Png_Decode Duplicate IHDR
d: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PNG with a duplicate IHDR chunk. Attackers can supply crafted PNGs via texture pack URLs or player skins so the unreset bufferIdx underflows remaining space, letting IDAT data overflow the buffer to crash clients or execute code.

t: @scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 Code Injection via TypeCompiler Schema Strings
d: @scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying crafted schema strings. Attackers can inject single-quote breakouts into string format, Kind names, property keys or Literal values to run arbitrary JavaScript in the host Node.js process during Compile() and Check().

t: Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 Remote Code Execution via NUL Byte
d: Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a file mask bypass vulnerability allowing attackers to upload restricted files via an embedded NUL byte in Upload Link filenames. Attackers can plant a Lua session file with a chosen UID and send a matching UID cookie to execute operating system commands as the service account.

t: Daptin: Broken Access Control (IDOR) in the generic YJS collaboration endpoint
d: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generic GET /yjs/:documentName WebSocket route in InitializeYjsResources requires a session but does not authorize the database resource selected by a typename.referenceId.columnName room name. The YJS initial-content provider then reads the selected file.* column without CanRead or CanUpdate checks, and bidirectional synchronization allows a low-privileged authenticated user to read or modify restricted row content. Unauthenticated requests are rejected, and standalone non-canonical room names remain shared-by-name rooms. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentication bypass attack due to improper handling of authentication. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and perform unauthorized actions within the context of the application. This is MTLVULN-1877.

t: Daptin: Unauthenticated SQL Injection via the `sort` query parameter on every entity list endpoint
d: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. Prior to 0.12.30, the generic GET /api/{entity} list endpoint accepts attacker-controlled sort values in PaginatedFindAllWithoutFilters in server/resource/resource_findallpaginated.go without validating the requested column against the table schema. The code uses those values for SELECT and ORDER BY identifier construction, so an embedded identifier quote can terminate the quoted identifier and make the remainder parse as SQL, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to extract unauthorized table data through blind or error-based behavior or repeatedly trigger query failures. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content, to conduct an unauthorized access attack due to improper authentication mechanisms. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. This is MTLVULN-1863.

t: Aperi'Solve: Uncontrolled resource consumption in PNG "repair" (PCRT): a sub-100-byte upload pins a worker CPU (DoS)
d: Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform. Prior to 3.4.2, an unauthenticated user can submit a PNG to POST /upload, which reaches aperisolve/utils/png.py through analyze_image, PCRTAnalyzer, PNG.repair(), and check_idat(). A malformed IDAT chunk can make attacker-controlled length and newline data drive an unbounded combinations search in PNG._fix_dos2unix(), causing repeated CRC checks that occupy a worker and delay or block image analysis for other users. Per-IP upload limits and eventual job termination bound the denial of service, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.2.

t: Bolt: Open redirect enables post-authentication redirection to arbitrary domains
d: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, LoginFormAuthenticator accepts unsafe destinations for the login success redirect and login failure redirect. An attacker can direct a user to an attacker-controlled domain after authentication succeeds or fails, enabling phishing and potential token theft. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

t: Bolt: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in URL-upload and embed endpoints
d: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the authenticated URL-upload endpoint and authenticated embed endpoint fetch user-supplied URLs server-side without protection against internal targets, allowing an attacker with the applicable backend permission to cause the Bolt server to request those targets. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

t: Bolt: Information disclosure through unfiltered public relation API endpoint
d: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the public Relation API lacks an access-control filter. Unauthenticated users can query its REST endpoints and GraphQL endpoints to discover metadata about unpublished, draft, and viewless content. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

t: Validation bypass of Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data
d: When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting in field values not being validated. The __init__() method of Pydantic V1 dataclasses stores all the provided keyword arguments in the instance __dict__ before validation, so a __pydantic_initialised__ keyword argument overrides the internal flag used to skip validation of already validated instances. As a result, data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data. The issue was fixed in Pydantic 1.10.27. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

t: Bolt ListFormatHelper SQL injection
d: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, SQL injection in ListFormatHelper allows authenticated users with upload permission to execute arbitrary SQL queries through /async/select-options and exfiltrate sensitive database contents when general/caching/list_format is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

t: Bolt: Prevent SSRF due to unchecked followed redirects
d: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.5, the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints validate only a submitted URL before fetching it server-side. The fetchers then follow redirects without revalidating each destination, allowing an authenticated user to bypass UrlSafetyChecker and cause the server to request internal or cloud-metadata addresses. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.5.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an arbitrary file upload attack due to insufficient file type validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system. This is MTLVULN-1861.

t: THC-Hydra through 9.7 Stack Buffer Overflow via hydra-http-form.c Cookie Handling
d: THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP UpdateFirmware requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29487.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP backend configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29063.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Wi-Fi Configuration Server Missing Authentication Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Wi-Fi Configuration Server Missing Authentication Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to modify Wi-Fi configuration on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of Wi-Fi configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29068.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Download of Code Without Integrity Check Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Download of Code Without Integrity Check Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. The issue results from the lack of proper verification of firmware integrity prior to installation. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28957.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A FTP URL Path Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A FTP URL Path Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the parsing of FTP URL paths during firmware updates. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28960.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. When parsing GetConfiguration requests, the process does not properly validate the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28968.

t: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
d: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the OCPP backend settings interface. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29056.

t: libXfont2 FreeType backend uninitialised strike_index out-of-bounds read
d: Use of uninitialized memory when processing certain font files in X.Org libXfont before 2.0.10 could be used by authenticated attackers to crash the X server.

t: HTSlib: Out-of-bounds read in HTSlib CRAM 3.x and 4.0 readers due to improper validation of input
d: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM BETA decoder functions cram_beta_decode_long, cram_beta_decode_int, and cram_beta_decode_char, and the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK functions cram_xpack_decode_long and cram_xpack_decode_int, have bounds-checking flaws caused by integer overflow after a multiplication. The resulting incorrect bounds check can allow decoding to read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially leaking process-state information or crashing the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

t: littlefs 2.8.0 through 2.11.3 Divide by Zero in lfs_mount_()
d: littlefs 2.8.0 through 2.11.3 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in lfs_mount_() that allows attackers to crash processes mounting crafted filesystem images when block_count is 0. Attackers can supply an image lacking a superblock entry or recording block_count 0, causing lfs->seed % lfs->block_count to trigger SIGFPE and denial of service.

t: Quasar before 2.35.3 DOM Clobbering Denial of Service via Native-Bridge Checks
d: Quasar before 2.35.3 contains a DOM clobbering vulnerability that allows attackers to break native wrapper detection by injecting HTML elements named Capacitor, cordova, or StatusBar. Attackers can place markup such as a div with id Capacitor into server-rendered or pre-rendered HTML so app.use(Quasar) throws and the application never mounts, or openURL() and AddressbarColor.set() throw.

t: Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 SSRF via Nextcloud Storage WebDAV Client
d: Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows space admins to reach internal hosts because Nextcloud.get_client builds WebDAV clients from Storage.url without calling safe_request. Attackers can create a NEXTCLOUD storage via POST /api/storage/ pointing at internal hosts, import a file, then call GET /api/get_recipe_file/<id>/ to read internal service or cloud metadata responses.

t: Stoatchat before 0.16.5 Memory Exhaustion via January /proxy JXL Decoding
d: Stoatchat before 0.16.5 contains an unbounded JXL image decoding vulnerability in revolt_files decode_image that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory via the january /proxy endpoint. Attackers can request a small hosted JXL file declaring 12000x12000 pixels through /proxy to trigger huge allocations, OOM-killing january and denying proxy and embed service.

t: Modoboa before 2.13.0 CRLF Injection via Relay Domain dkim_key_selector
d: Modoboa before 2.13.0 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability that allows Resellers or users with domain add or change permission to inject rspamd DKIM selector map entries by supplying an unvalidated dkim_key_selector through the relay domain API. Attackers can embed a carriage return in the selector to override another tenant's domain selector, causing rspamd to sign its outgoing mail with a nonexistent selector and fail DKIM verification.

t: Manyfold 0.124.0 before 0.154.2 SSRF via ActivityPub Actor Icon and Image URLs
d: Manyfold 0.124.0 before 0.154.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to make the instance fetch internal URLs by supplying malicious ActivityPub actor icon.url and image.url fields. Attackers can deliver Create or Update activities to the inbox, causing the Shrine remote_url plugin to request internal or cloud metadata hosts and store responses as creator avatar or banner attachments.

t: OpnForm before 2.8.2 Unauthorized Asset Move via StoreFormSubmissionJob::storeFile
d: OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to move other forms' shared assets by supplying their URLs in file upload fields. Attackers can submit a public form with another form's cover or logo URL, causing Storage::move() to relocate it into submissions and break that asset.

t: SABnzbd before 5.2.0 Path Traversal via NZB Propername and Episodename Metadata
d: SABnzbd before 5.2.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Sorter that allows attackers to write files outside the Complete folder via crafted propername, episodename or job name (%dn) values. Attackers can supply a malicious NZB with '...' sequences that collapse to '..' after single-pass replacement, moving downloaded files into arbitrary directories writable by SABnzbd.

t: OpnForm before 2.8.2 SSRF Guard Bypass via PublicWebhookUrl::isPublicIp
d: OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in PublicWebhookUrl::isPublicIp that fails to reject CGNAT, NAT64 and 6to4 address ranges. Authenticated users can configure webhook, form import or PDF image URLs resolving to these ranges to make the server send HTTPS requests to internal hosts.

t: diaspora* before 0.10.0 Stored XSS via OpenGraph og:video:secure_url
d: diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by crafting og:video:secure_url values. Attackers can post links to pages whose allowlisted-prefix video URL contains a quote and onload handler, executing script in readers' sessions when they click the video preview.

t: diaspora* before 0.10.0 XSS via maxheight in oEmbed endpoint
d: diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject iframe attributes via the maxheight parameter of the GET /oembed endpoint. Attackers can supply a single quote in maxheight to inject an onload handler into the returned html, executing script in third-party oEmbed consumers that embed it unsanitized.

t: node-soap before 1.14.1 Prototype Pollution via multiRef id in WSDL.xmlToObject
d: node-soap before 1.14.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in WSDL.xmlToObject that allows unauthenticated attackers to pollute Object.prototype via an XML element with id="__proto__". Attackers can send a single crafted SOAP request to a soap.listen() server, or return a malicious response to a client, causing all subsequent SOAP parsing to fail until process restart.

t: parse5-html-rewriting-stream 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 XSS via RewritingStream#emitText
d: parse5-html-rewriting-stream 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in RewritingStream#emitText, which skips escaping based on a stale lastStartTagName. Attackers can place entity-encoded markup after a closed script or style element to bypass RewritingStream-based filters and execute script in users' browsers.

t: modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 Local File Inclusion via shop_content.php
d: modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows administrators to include arbitrary server files by storing ../ sequences in the content manager file name. Unauthenticated requests to shop_content.php then pass the stored path to include(), executing embedded PHP in uploaded content files or images as the web server user.

t: parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 Denial of Service via Preprocessor#_processSurrogate
d: parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

t: modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 Reflected XSS via module Parameter in admin/support.php
d: modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin/support.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the module parameter. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted link to run script in the admin panel, reading CSRF tokens and changing shop settings.

t: modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 Stored XSS via products_name Field
d: modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows administrators with product editing permission to inject script via the products_name field. The unescaped name is rendered in the h1 heading of product detail and reviews pages, executing script in the browsers of shoppers and logged-in customers.

t: HTSlib: Heap write overflow in HTSlib FASTA index handling
d: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, fai_retrieve does not verify that the line width recorded in a FASTA .fai index is greater than or equal to the number of bases per line. When the line width is exactly one less than the base count, retrieval allocates an undersized heap buffer and writes one byte beyond its end; larger discrepancies instead cause an allocation failure that is handled. This issue can corrupt heap memory and crash the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

t: HTSlib: Stack write overflow in HTSlib CRAM decoder
d: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM decoder validates the 254-character query-name limit only after decoding the name into a 1024-byte stack array. An attacker-controlled CRAM record can provide an overlong query name and overflow the local stack buffer before the later validation runs; all CRAM format versions are affected. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt stack data, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.
