Workqueue: o2net o2net_rx_until_empty [ocfs2_nodemanager] RIP: 0010:0xffffffffc0423871 [Instruction byte dump omitted.] Register dump omitted. Call Trace: <TASK> ? o2net_rx_until_empty+0x19b1/0x3300 [ocfs2_nodemanager] ? __pfx_o2net_rx_until_empty+0x10/0x10 [ocfs2_nodemanager] ? lock_acquire+0x190/0x300 ? process_one_work+0x935/0x1b40 ? process_one_work+0x834/0x1b40 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? lock_release+0xc8/0x290 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? process_one_work+0x9a8/0x1b40 ? __pfx_process_one_work+0x10/0x10 ? lock_acquire+0x190/0x300 ? lock_is_held_type+0x8f/0x100 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? worker_thread+0x65c/0xe40 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __kthread_parkme+0x177/0x220 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __pfx_worker_thread+0x10/0x10 ? kthread+0x351/0x460 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __pfx_kthread+0x10/0x10 ? ret_from_fork+0x659/0x940 ? __pfx_ret_from_fork+0x10/0x10 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __switch_to+0x74f/0xf70 ? __pfx_kthread+0x10/0x10 ? ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30 </TASK> Modules linked in: ocfs2_nodemanager [last unloaded: ocfs2_dlm] ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---

t: ocfs2: drain quorum work before removing the cluster
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ocfs2: drain quorum work before removing the cluster The configured cluster must remain available until an in-flight quorum decision has finished using its fencing method. o2quo_make_decision() drops qs_lock before calling o2quo_fence_self(), which marks heartbeat regions for unclean stop and then reads o2nm_single_cluster->cl_fence_method. Cluster removal clears the singleton without waiting for this independent system-workqueue item. When a failed-quorum decision overlaps removal of the heartbeat regions, nodes and cluster through configfs, the worker can be preempted after marking the regions and resume after the singleton has been cleared: Quorum worker Configfs removal select fence; drop qs_lock o2hb_stop_all_regions() remove regions; join heartbeat threads remove nodes; stop o2net clear singleton; release cluster read cl_fence_method The resumed read dereferences NULL instead of applying the configured fencing method. The heartbeat thread's dependency protects the local node only until the thread exits, and draining o2net does not wait for qs_work. Add o2quo_flush_work() to drain pending or running quorum decisions before clearing the singleton in o2nm_cluster_group_drop_item(). By this point the heartbeat regions and nodes have been removed, so their work publishers are stopped. The worker can finish while the cluster and its configured fencing method remain available. It does not acquire the configfs mutex held by the removal path. Keep o2quo_exit() as the counterpart of o2quo_init() for module teardown and initialization failure, and have it call the same drain helper. Cluster removal uses only the explicitly named drain operation. KASAN report as below: Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc000000011b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000008d8-0x00000000000008df] CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 72 Comm: kworker/0:2 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc4-next-20260921-pmb-ocfs2-functional-v1+ #1 PREEMPT(lazy) Hardware name: QEMU Ubuntu 24.04 PC v2 (i440FX + PIIX, arch_caps fix, 1996), BIOS 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2 04/01/2014 Workqueue: events o2quo_make_decision RIP: 0010:o2quo_fence_self+0x65/0x200 Register dump omitted. Call Trace: <TASK> o2quo_make_decision+0x345/0x3a0 ? __pfx_o2quo_make_decision+0x10/0x10 ? process_one_work+0x834/0x1b40 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? lock_release+0xc8/0x290 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 process_one_work+0x9a8/0x1b40 ? __pfx_process_one_work+0x10/0x10 ? lock_acquire+0x190/0x300 ? lock_is_held_type+0x8f/0x100 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 worker_thread+0x65c/0xe40 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __kthread_parkme+0x177/0x220 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __pfx_worker_thread+0x10/0x10 kthread+0x351/0x460 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __pfx_kthread+0x10/0x10 ret_from_fork+0x659/0x940 ? __pfx_ret_from_fork+0x10/0x10 ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5 ? __switch_to+0x74f/0xf70 ? __pfx_kthread+0x10/0x10 ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30 </TASK> Modules linked in: ---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---

t: ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files The OCFS2 debugfs file operation tables do not set owner. The full debugfs proxy obtains real_fops with fops_get() at open and keeps it until final release. Without an owner, this does not acquire a reference to the module containing the table and its callbacks. Removing the debugfs entries does not drain retained open files. An open connected_nodes file can therefore outlive ocfs2_nodemanager and make full_proxy_release() read real_fops->release from freed module memory. Heming also reproduced the issue with fs_state and asked for the other OCFS2 debugfs operation tables to be checked. Set owner to THIS_MODULE in all eleven explicit debugfs operation tables: five in ocfs2_nodemanager, four in ocfs2_dlm, and two in ocfs2. The existing debugfs get/put pair then holds the appropriate module until final release. Leave the open, read and release callbacks unchanged. The blockcheck table already sets owner through DEFINE_DEBUGFS_ATTRIBUTE(), so it needs no change. The original controlled test used an unloadable OCFS2 module and case-local probe filters without changing the candidate open, unload or release logic. Closing a retained connected_nodes file after normal unload produced: BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfff804cfef Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI RIP: 0010:full_proxy_release+0xbf/0x190 Call Trace: <TASK> __fput+0x39a/0xa60 fput_close_sync+0xff/0x200 __x64_sys_close+0x8c/0xf0 do_syscall_64+0x114/0x620 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK> Modules linked in: [last unloaded: ocfs2_nodemanager]

t: smb: client: do not pass a NULL buf to is_oplock_break()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: do not pass a NULL buf to is_oplock_break() receive_encrypted_read() sets *num_mids = 1 and never writes the caller's bufs[]. Offload returns -1 with *num_mids = 0, so the demultiplex thread skips the frame. The inline decrypt path returns 0 even when smb2_find_mid() fails. cifs_demultiplex_thread() then treats mids[i] == NULL as an oplock break and calls is_oplock_break(bufs[i], server) with bufs[i] still NULL. smb2_is_valid_oplock_break() reads hdr.Command at offset 12 and oopses. A large encrypted READ whose MessageId does not match is enough to panic cifsd. Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f] CPU: 0 PID: 100 Comm: cifsd RIP: smb2_is_valid_oplock_break+0xc8/0x2270 [cifs] cifs_demultiplex_thread Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception Return -1 when inline decrypt finds no mid, and skip is_oplock_break() plus the unknown-frame dump when bufs[i] is NULL. receive_encrypted_standard() already assigns bufs[*num_mids].

t: smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race Currently, init_cifs() calls cifs_proc_init() near the beginning of the function, before INIT_LIST_HEAD, leading to a momentarily uninitialized, but exposed, procfs. If a userspace process reads this empty procfs, iterating over a zeroed list_head leads to a NULL pointer dereference and a kernel oops/panic. For example, if a delay is added between cifs_proc_init() and INIT_LIST_HEAD, and a userspace process is polling /proc/fs/cifs/DebugData, the following oops occurs: BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000608 Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP PTI CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 3477 Comm: cat Not tainted 7.3.0-02212-g4df4d2a577db-dirty #6 PREEMPT(lazy) RIP: 0010:cifs_debug_data_proc_show+0x103/0xd80 [cifs] Call Trace: <TASK> ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400 seq_read_iter+0x183/0x400 proc_reg_read_iter+0x62/0x90 copy_splice_read+0x215/0x310 splice_file_to_pipe+0xec/0x1c0 do_splice+0x4b8/0x780 __se_sys_splice+0x18f/0x250 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x330 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK> Fix this by moving cifs_proc_init() down in init_cifs(), ensuring it runs only after all internal lists, locks, counters, and workqueues are fully ready, but before registering the filesystem. Update the error cleanup ladder and exit_cifs() to maintain proper LIFO order.

t: thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not guaranteed numerically sorted). I initially noticed this issue on a Dell XPS9720 when the system would seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I tried multiple kernel versions including v7.2.7 and v7.3-rc4 to see if that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()` walk that I ultimately ended up changing. To confirm this issue, I did an eBPF trace of `bus_for_each_dev()`, `complete_rpm()`, and `complete()` while unplugging in a variety of situations and found that an unplug from domain 0 tries to `complete_rpm()` domain 1's switch, whose RPM completion is not initialized and thus is holding a null wait-list pointer, triggering the page fault. Here are the key sections of that eBPF trace. Note that HEAD denotes the completion's own wait-list HEAD: ``` RESCAN_ENTER domain=0 COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=0-1 target_domain=0 route=0x1 parent=0-0 unplugged=1 COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=HEAD prev=HEAD BUS_WALK domain=0 start=0-1 callback=complete_rpm CALLBACK_ENTER rescan_domain=0 dev=1-0 parent=domain1 is_switch=1 COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=1-0 target_domain=1 route=0x0 parent=domain1 unplugged=0 COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=0 prev=0 complete+5 complete_rpm+43 bus_for_each_dev+133 icm_free_unplugged_children+250 icm_rescan_work+42 ``` This patch gates the `complete()` on an additional condition - that the Thunderbolt domain matches the domain of the device that was unplugged. I only have a single system with multiple Thunderbolt domains - the Dell XPS9720. I am consistently able to reproduce the Oops on that system. Since running with this patch, I have not seen the Oops reoccur. I have also tested it on a Thinkpad X1-Gen12, and that system boots and runs well with it, but it only has a single Thunderbolt domain, so it does not exercise the multi-domain failure case.

t: net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released. Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero. Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still holds the filter. The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately. Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to determine whether the classifier has become empty. Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference. This fix does not add fields, snapshots, or per-filter memory.

t: driver core: take parent lock on deferred probe
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: driver core: take parent lock on deferred probe USB interfaces should be probed with the parent USB device lock held, but this is not honoured when probe is deferred. Add a new bus_probe_device_deferred() helper to handle deferred probe where the parent device lock is not held.

t: Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as potentially malicious. hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too: the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than the ring. The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices, hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO. One re-read of write_index is left unchecked in this patch: hv_get_ring_bufferindices() fetches it again for the prev_indices trailer. The value is only returned to the host and is not used as an offset or length for indexing. Since this is not a security issue, it is addressed later in the series. Open-coding the bytes available arithmetic keeps the fix free of prerequisites; a later patch refactors it into a helper function.

t: backlight: qcom-wled: Fix NULL pointer dereference in wled_remove()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: backlight: qcom-wled: Fix NULL pointer dereference in wled_remove() wled_probe() doesn't set the driver data for the platform device. As a result, platform_get_drvdata() in wled_remove() will return NULL, and the first dereference of it crashes on unbind. Set the platform device driver data in wled_probe().

t: ksmbd: deny access for an empty DACL instead of granting the request
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: deny access for an empty DACL instead of granting the request smb_check_perm_dacl() returns the access mask it computes to the SMB2 CREATE handler, which uses it as the granted access for the open. For a security descriptor whose DACL is present but contains no ACEs, the function is supposed to deny access: an empty (non-NULL) DACL grants no access to anyone except the object owner's implicit READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC (MS-DTYP 2.4.5). The empty-DACL branch only denies when both - the DACL has no trailing bytes (pdacl_size == sizeof(struct smb_acl)), and - the request contains bits beyond READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC. In every other case it takes the shared "goto err_out" with rc still 0, which returns success without modifying *pdaccess, so the caller grants the full requested access. Three problems follow: - The READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC carve-out models the owner's implicit rights, but the check runs before is_owner is computed, so those rights are handed to *every* caller, not just the owner. For READ_CONTROL the SMB2 CREATE path does not fall back to inode_permission(), so any user can read the security descriptor of an object whose empty DACL is meant to deny them. - A request of exactly READ_CONTROL and/or WRITE_DAC is granted to any caller. WRITE_DAC lets the handle rewrite the DACL. - A DACL that declares zero ACEs but carries trailing bytes (pdacl_size > sizeof(struct smb_acl)) skips the deny entirely and is granted whatever was requested. On shares where the NT ACL is the authoritative access control -- e.g. "force user" shares, where every client maps to one POSIX identity so POSIX cannot distinguish users -- this is an access-control bypass. Compute is_owner before the empty-DACL branch and deny access from an empty DACL unless the caller is the owner requesting no more than READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC.

t: ksmbd: fix OOB read and cross-share confusion in ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix OOB read and cross-share confusion in ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect() ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect() indexes ab_pathname[share->path_sz + 1] without checking that the path is longer than share->path_sz + 1 (d_path() fills the buffer from the end). A durable fp is not bound to its original share, so a client can preserve a file from a short-path share and reconnect it on a long-path share, making strcmp() read past the PATH_MAX buffer - with a long enough share path this oopses the kernel, and on a mapped page it also gives a byte-equality oracle on adjacent heap (the reconnect succeeds exactly when the out-of-bounds string equals the requested name). A same-share variant with the durable fp at the share root reads 1 byte past the buffer (strlen(ab_pathname) == share->path_sz). Check before comparing: the path must be longer than share->path_sz, it must start with share->path, and the next character must be '/'. The share root itself is accepted only for an empty name.

t: ksmbd: fix parent dentry lifetime in directory enumeration
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix parent dentry lifetime in directory enumeration ksmbd_populate_dot_dotdot_entries() builds the ".." entry from the open directory's d_parent and passes that pointer to ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs() without taking a reference. That pointer is only valid while the directory stays under this parent. If a concurrent rename moves the directory elsewhere, the old parent loses its last reference; a following rmdir then turns it into a negative dentry with d_inode cleared, and after the RCU grace period the dentry itself is freed. The worker still holds the raw pointer and dereferences d_inode through vfs_getattr() and vfs_getxattr(). A remote SMB client, authenticated or guest, triggers this by listing a directory while that directory is moved under a new parent and the old parent is deleted. It can be done by the client itself with write access or by other concurrent writers, triggering null-ptr-deref and slab-use-after-free on a KASAN build. KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007] Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work RIP: 0010:xattr_permission+0x9d/0x160 Call Trace: vfs_getxattr+0x9c/0x1b0 ksmbd_vfs_getxattr+0x82/0x100 ksmbd_vfs_get_dos_attrib_xattr+0x7f/0x130 ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs+0x435/0x650 ksmbd_populate_dot_dotdot_entries+0x25e/0x630 smb2_query_dir+0xcf9/0x1a20 handle_ksmbd_work+0x5f1/0x1c80 process_one_work+0x90b/0x19d0 Fix by using the dentry reference counting APIs: take the parent with dget_parent(), take a matching dget() on ".", and dput() the dentry once ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs() has returned or the pattern does not match.

t: ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP A compound request can place SESSION_SETUP after another command. That earlier command leaves a reference to its session in work->sess. smb2_sess_setup() then overwrites work->sess with the session it looks up or creates, and the dispatcher later puts work->sess only once. The inherited reference is never dropped. That leaks the session, together with its setup connection and socket, and every repeat of the compound leaks another. unreferenced object (size 512): __kmalloc_cache_noprof+0x32c/0x3a0 ksmbd_smb2_session_create+0xf6/0x9c0 [ksmbd] smb2_sess_setup+0xda4/0x6280 [ksmbd] handle_ksmbd_work+0x88c/0x1cb0 [ksmbd] Save the inherited session on entry. After the request has been processed, release it once, but only when smb2_sess_setup() has replaced work->sess with its own session or cleared it. Do this after ksmbd_conn_unlock() so the put does not run under srv_mutex. An error path may instead leave the inherited session in work->sess. Keep it there, so the dispatcher still puts it and the error response is still signed or encrypted with it as before.

t: ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces With no interface list configured, ksmbd binds every interface that comes up. ksmbd_netdev_event() does not look at the device's namespace, and create_socket() opens the listener in the namespace of the task raising NETDEV_UP. A container with its own address on a bridge brings up its interface and finds port 445 in its namespace already taken by ksmbd, so an SMB server running inside the container fails with "Address already in use". Interfaces are also matched by name only, so a container's eth0 going down would stop the listener on the host's eth0. Only handle netdev events for devices in init_net.

t: ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open A write-only client can open an existing named stream with FILE_OPEN_IF without permission to read the underlying file. The case-insensitive lookup finds the xattr name, but querying its value length then fails with -EACCES. smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() treats every negative result as a missing stream and replaces the existing xattr with an empty value. A failed xattr list is not proof that the stream is absent either: for example, -ENOMEM can lead to the same empty replacement. Preserve listing errors and create a stream only for -ENOENT or -ENODATA. The latter can occur if the xattr is removed between listing its name and querying its value. Return other lookup errors without changing the stream. A write-only FILE_OPEN now reports access denied instead of name not found. FILE_OVERWRITE_IF and FILE_SUPERSEDE on an unreadable stream also fail instead of appearing to replace it. Stream writes and EOF changes already need to read the old value, so such handles cannot update the stream after opening either.

t: ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests A failed multichannel binding can retain its target session on the work item so that the error response can be signed. Subsequent compound commands can then use that session together with a tree connection left over from an earlier command. Limit binding SESSION_SETUP requests to standalone messages during message validation, before smb2_sess_setup() can replace work->sess. Check both NextCommand and the current request offset to cover binding in the first, middle and last positions of a compound. The existing validation error path returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and stops processing the remaining commands. This intentionally limits support for compounded binding. It is not a protocol requirement that binding be standalone. Standalone binding and non-binding compounds retain their existing behavior, without changing session, tree or response encryption handling.

t: ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths A FileLinkInformation request can supply "/" as the new link name. smb2_get_name() strips the trailing slash and passes an empty string to ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing(). ksmbd_vfs_path_lookup() resolves an empty pathname as the configured share path, without LOOKUP_BENEATH. With ReplaceIfExists set, smb2_create_link() can therefore remove the share root from its parent before link creation fails. An authenticated client with a writable share and DELETE access to a file can trigger this if the share root is empty and the mapped user has write and search permission on its parent directory. Return -EINVAL for empty pathnames when for_remove is set, before resolving the share path or acquiring removal resources. Ordinary lookups continue to accept empty pathnames for opening the share root.

t: ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests Initialize the compatibility byte in request buffers without zeroing the entire allocation. Keep the one-byte compatibility exception for SMB2 messages so valid zero-length WRITE requests remain compatible, and validate the data range in the WRITE handlers against the current compound request before accessing it. This prevents stale request-buffer data from being written to files or sent to IPC pipes.

t: MISP CryptographicKey: Revoked PGP Keys Still Validate Protected Event Signatures and Key Revocation Sync Is Ineffective
d: MISP, a threat intelligence sharing platform, contains a vulnerability in its cryptographic key management for protected (PGP-signed) events. Two related defects allow a revoked PGP key to remain effective for signing and validating protected events. First, the validateProtectedEvent() method in the CryptographicKey model iterates over the event's stored cryptographic keys to verify a PGP signature but does not check the revoked flag on each key. A key explicitly marked as revoked is still used to validate signatures, meaning an entity whose key has been revoked can continue to sign protected events and have them accepted by the MISP instance. Second, the captureCryptographicKeyUpdate() method, responsible for synchronizing the key list when a sync user edits a protected event, contained a query bug (find('first') instead of find('all')) that caused only the first stored key to be considered. As a result, revocations of additional keys were never persisted, keys absent from the pushed list were not removed, and entries lacking an explicit fingerprint were mismatched and incorrectly deleted. Additionally, the revocation logic did not enforce the invariant that a revocation, once stored, is never lifted by subsequent pushes. A third minor issue: a signed protected event submitted without any cryptographic keys triggered an unhandled 500 error rather than a proper rejection response. Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated sync user with permission to add or edit protected events on the MISP instance. The impact is that revoked keys retain signing authority, key revocations propagated by sync partners are silently dropped, and the integrity of the protected-event trust chain is compromised. In a multi-instance MISP deployment, events signed by revoked keys can propagate to other instances, extending the integrity impact across the sync network.

t: ksmbd: validate AppInstanceId takeover target
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: validate AppInstanceId takeover target AppInstanceId lookup currently selects the first open with the matching identifier. CREATE for an unrelated share or path can therefore force-close another session's open before authorization of the new target. Matching only the base path also conflates alternate data streams with the unnamed stream. MS-SMB2 requires the old open to match the share and path, belong to a different ClientGuid, and be closed only when the requester has GENERIC_READ access. Search all opens with the ID and match share, resolved path, stream, and the current connection's client GUID. Retain a share configuration reference in ksmbd_file and reuse its name instead of allocating a name for every open. This keeps matching safe during tree connection teardown and preserves name-based matching across configuration updates. Refresh the share reference on durable reconnect and restore the old reference if reopening fails. Serialize connection and share comparisons with durable disconnect/reconnect, and recheck the target before closing it. Keep the original ClientGuid for durable replay and lease checks. Check AppInstanceVersion before querying access, even when GENERIC_READ is absent, and before disconnected delete-on-close cleanup. Rejected CREATE must leave other durable opens untouched. Calculate maximal access on the matched open's referenced path so a rename cannot substitute another file's authorization. Require read access with the effective VFS credentials as well as the NT DACL before takeover. Access denial only skips takeover and leaves CREATE to its normal access checks. Restore filesystem credentials before returning a takeover error. Handle takeover before checking FILE_CREATE collisions, and re-resolve the path after closing the old open. This lets delete-on-close remove the old file before a new one is created. Include SYNCHRONIZE in the baseline maximal-access mask so read-only files report GENERIC_READ correctly.

t: ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic parse_sec_desc() constructs SID and DACL pointers by adding untrusted 32-bit offsets to the security descriptor before checking their bounds. The existing checks reject offsets into the descriptor header, but do not reject offsets beyond the descriptor's length. On a 32-bit kernel, a large offset can wrap the pointer before the descriptor. The end-only checks in parse_sid() and parse_dacl() can then accept it, allowing an authenticated SMB2 SET_INFO request to access memory outside the security descriptor and fault the kernel. Check each nonzero offset against acl_len before constructing its pointer. Initialize the optional owner and group SID pointers to NULL so an omitted SID remains absent when parsing the DACL.

t: ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header When an encrypted request comes in, the decryption key is picked by the SessionId in the transform header, but the request is then authorized under whatever session the decrypted inner header names. Nothing ever compares the two, so on a connection with more than one session a client can get a request decrypted with one session's key and run it as another session. Encrypted requests are exempt from signing too, so a valid AEAD tag is the only proof of session identity, and it is checked against the wrong session. MS-SMB2 says the server must check that the transform SessionId matches the one in the decrypted SMB2 header and treat a mismatch as a protocol error. Add that check in __handle_ksmbd_work() after decryption, before dispatching: the message has to be at least one fixed SMB2 header, the first operation must not set SMB2_FLAGS_RELATED_OPERATIONS and its SessionId must match the transform SessionId, and every following non-related operation in a compound chain must carry the same SessionId. NextCommand offsets must be 8-byte aligned and stay inside the message; the bounds check is done by subtraction so it cannot wrap. When the decrypted payload is a compression transform, the existing decompression step runs first and the decompressed SMB2 message is checked instead, since a compression transform header carries no SessionId.

t: cgroup: serialize migrations of newly forked processes
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cgroup: serialize migrations of newly forked processes With favordynmods enabled, a cgroup.procs migration takes the target threadgroup's cgroup_threadgroup_rwsem for writing. A process fork holds the forking threadgroup's semaphore for reading. These are different semaphores when fork creates a new process. copy_process() publishes the child's PID before cgroup_post_fork() links the child to its css_set. A writer can find the child in that interval, take its uncontended semaphore, and migrate it while child->cgroups still points to init_css_set and child->cg_list is empty. Migration links the node into init_css_set.mg_tasks. cgroup_post_fork() then adds the same node to the intended css_set as though it were unlinked, corrupting both task lists and their css_set ownership. This regresses the fork/migration race fixed by commit b12b533fa523 ("cgroups: add lock for child->cgroups in cgroup_post_fork()") and restored again in 2012 after the lock had been removed. The old task_lock protection was later superseded by global css_set and cgroup threadgroup locking. The change identified by the Fixes tag narrowed only the migration side back to a per-threadgroup lock, recreating the different-process exclusion failure. Take the new threadgroup's semaphore for reading before the child becomes visible and hold it through cgroup_post_fork(). Use a nested lock subclass because fork already holds the parent's semaphore. CLONE_THREAD children share the parent's signal_struct and remain covered by the existing lock. Migrations of unrelated, fully initialized threadgroups remain concurrent. An AI coding assistant was used to identify and reproduce the regression and to develop and test this fix.

t: wifi: b43: fix use-after-free in b43_bcma_remove()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: wifi: b43: fix use-after-free in b43_bcma_remove() b43_one_core_detach() frees the struct b43_wldev it is given the bus device of. b43_bcma_remove() then reads wldev->dev again to free the bus device, which is a read of freed memory. b43_ssb_remove() does not have the problem: it takes a copy of wldev->dev at the start. Do the same here.

t: SUNRPC: fix netns use-after-free in write_gssp()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: fix netns use-after-free in write_gssp() While fuzzing with a customized syzkaller, I hit a refcount warning in xprt_alloc(), reached from a write to /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy: refcount_t: addition on 0; use-after-free. WARNING: lib/refcount.c:25 at refcount_warn_saturate+0xf8/0x120 CPU: 0 PID: 10404 Comm: syz.0.17 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc1-00096-gcfebfd3db73d Call Trace: <TASK> xprt_alloc+0x83f/0x9d0 xs_setup_xprt+0xaf/0x3c0 xs_setup_local+0x47/0x7f0 xprt_create_transport+0x16c/0x730 rpc_create+0x38e/0x7f0 gssp_rpc_create+0xe2/0x180 set_gssp_clnt+0xba/0x1b0 write_gssp+0x200/0x310 proc_reg_write+0x240/0x330 vfs_write+0x2aa/0x1050 ksys_write+0x12a/0x250 do_syscall_64+0x117/0x750 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK> create_use_gss_proxy_proc_entry() stores the struct net pointer as the proc entry's private data without taking a reference on it, and an open file descriptor does not pin the namespace either, as procfs only pins the proc_dir_entry. write_gssp() reads that pointer back with pde_data() and hands it to set_gssp_clnt(), which reaches xprt_init(): xprt->xprt_net = get_net_track(net, &xprt->ns_tracker, GFP_KERNEL); get_net_track() -> get_net() -> refcount_inc() is unconditional, so rpc_create() assumes its caller holds a reference on args.net. write_gssp() does not. Dropping the last ns.count reference does not make the file go away. __put_net() only queues cleanup_net() on a workqueue, and the remove_proc_entry() that fences off further writes runs from the rpcsec_gss pernet .exit method, that is, from inside cleanup_net(). A write landing between those two points increments a refcount that is already zero. cleanup_net() does not re-read ns.count, so the namespace is freed anyway and the rpc_xprt -- along with the AF_LOCAL socket opened for it -- is left pointing at freed memory. The resurrected count is visible to the rest of that teardown too: with CONFIG_IPV6_MROUTE the same cleanup_net() worker then trips !mr_can_free_table() in ip6mr_free_table(), which tests check_net() on the namespace it is freeing. It reduces to opening /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy inside a new network namespace, calling setns() back to the original one to drop the last reference, and then writing "1" to the still-open descriptor. Take the reference in write_gssp() itself and refuse the write when the namespace is already gone. This is what procfs does for every other /proc/net file: get_proc_net() is maybe_get_net(PDE_NET(PDE(inode))) and seq_open_net() returns -ENXIO when it fails. PDE_NET() cannot be reused here because the parent directory /proc/net/rpc carries no namespace pointer. Adding a .pre_exit to rpcsec_gss_net_ops so the entry is removed earlier would only narrow the window, since pre_exit also runs from cleanup_net(). Live namespaces are unaffected: a write still returns the error from set_gssp_clnt(), a write of "2" still returns -EINVAL, and reads are untouched.

t: spmi: Fix potential use-after-free by grabbing of_node reference
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: spmi: Fix potential use-after-free by grabbing of_node reference As noticed by Sashiko during a review run of an unrelated patch, in of_spmi_register_devices(), for_each_available_child_of_node() is used to loop through children, and to also assign a node to a newly created SPMI child device. Problem is that the refcount is dropped at every iteration so, in the specific case of DT overlays, a use-after-free may occur when an overlay is dynamically unloaded! To resolve this, increase the of_node refcount when assigning (in function of_spmi_register_devices) and release the reference in spmi_device_remove().

t: Double free during DOM XML serialization
d: Double free during DOM XML serialization. The XML serializer of Dom\XMLDocument and Dom\HTMLDocument can share ownership of a generated namespace prefix between the namespace-prefix maps of an element and a descendant, so the prefix is used after being freed and then freed a second time. The document does not need to be malformed. An application that parses attacker-controlled XML or HTML with these classes and serializes it with saveXml() can be crashed, and repeated requests can cause denial of service. Code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue affects PHP versions 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: smb: client: fix use-after-free infoleak via the readdir resume name
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix use-after-free infoleak via the readdir resume name CIFSFindNext() copies the resume name that cifs_save_resume_key() recorded from the last entry of the previous response into its request; psrch_inf->presume_name points into the response buffer that entry came from, and nothing ever clears it. find_cifs_entry() records a new name only from a response with a usable last entry, and cifs_readdir() only from an entry it walks to, so a response that carries no entries and leaves last_entry NULL, because CIFSFindFirst() or CIFSFindNext() rejected LastNameOffset, refreshes neither and presume_name keeps pointing into the previous response. That buffer has already been released: by CIFSFindNext() before it installs the new response, or by find_cifs_entry() when it rewinds the search, which does not drop the name either and can then fail in initiate_cifs_search() before a new response replaces it. The next CIFSFindNext() then copies up to PATH_MAX - 1 bytes of the resume name out of the released buffer into its request and sends them to the server: a use-after-free read that leaks kernel memory to a malicious or compromised server, which can provoke it with a single FindNext response that carries no entries and a LastNameOffset above CIFSMaxBufSize, which is all the existing check rejects. With KASAN enabled, a server that answers a listing that way gives: CIFS: VFS: ignoring corrupt resume name ================================================================== BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in CIFSFindNext+0x8ca/0x14c0 Read of size 4080 at addr ffff88807c823f98 by task ls/83 CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 83 Comm: ls Tainted: G B 7.3.0-rc4-00457-gf14572c203d5 #69 PREEMPT(lazy) Tainted: [B]=BAD_PAGE Call Trace: <TASK> kasan_report+0xdf/0x1a0 kasan_check_range+0x10f/0x1e0 __asan_memcpy+0x23/0x60 CIFSFindNext+0x8ca/0x14c0 cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0 iterate_dir+0x1c0/0x570 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x133/0x270 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x5d0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK> Allocated by task 83 on cpu 1 at 13.497119s: cifs_buf_get+0x36/0x90 smb_init+0x4f/0x110 CIFSFindNext+0xf7/0x14c0 cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0 Freed by task 83 on cpu 0 at 13.584018s: cifs_buf_release+0x41/0x80 CIFSFindNext+0xfce/0x14c0 cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0 The buggy address is located 16280 bytes inside of freed 16588-byte region [ffff88807c820000, ffff88807c8240cc) ================================================================== The same memcpy() first reads past the end of that object while it is still live, a slab-out-of-bounds read that the following patches bound; that is the taint the report above carries. SMB1 is not negotiated by default; reaching this code requires an explicit vers=1.0 mount. Clear presume_name and resume_name_len whenever a new response is installed and when the rewind path releases the search buffer, so that the name never outlives the buffer it points into, and reset resume_key with them, since it was taken from the same entry and would otherwise be sent with an empty name. A response without a usable last entry then continues the search with an empty resume name rather than a stale one; CIFSFindNext() skips the copy of a zero-length name so that it never runs on the NULL pointer. The next patch in the series leaves last_entry NULL for a response that carries no entries, and bounds LastNameOffset against the received response rather than against CIFSMaxBufSize. Responses that are given a last entry today then take the path fixed here, so that patch must not be applied without this one.

t: smb: client: fix use-after-free in cifs_ses_add_channel()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix use-after-free in cifs_ses_add_channel() The error path of cifs_ses_add_channel() calls cifs_put_tcp_session() before cifs_chan_clear_need_reconnect(). The latter reaches cifs_ses_get_chan_index(), which dereferences server->terminate; if the put was the final reference, TCP_Server_Info is already freed and this is a use-after-free. Same put-then-use pattern as the recently fixed sibling in commit 717e0a25036b ("cifs: Fix server use-after-free in cifs_chan_skip_or_disable()"). Move the put last, but do not read chan->server after dropping chan_lock: chan points into ses->chans[], and once chan_count is decremented a concurrent add_channel can reuse the slot and overwrite the pointer, so the put would act on the new channel's server. Cache the pointer under chan_lock, clear the reconnect bit and decrement chan_count while still holding the reference, and release it after the unlock. This issue was discovered by Tencent CodeBuddy Security.

t: sched_ext: Fix use-after-free of a local reenq node left on an inactive cpu
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sched_ext: Fix use-after-free of a local reenq node left on an inactive cpu A local DSQ reenq is queued on the rq through a per-sched node and run from deferred work. When the reenq is requested from dispatch, the work is a balance callback queued once dispatch is done. A cpu going down installs balance push early in its teardown, and queue_balance_callback() refuses new callbacks from then on. ops.dispatch() keeps running on that cpu until the rq goes offline after an RCU grace period, so a reenq it requests in that window may never run. The IMMED handling in dispatch_one() requests one the same way. A reenq requested from elsewhere for a cpu that is already offline goes through irq_work_queue_on(), which warns, and its work doesn't run until the cpu comes back. Either way the node stays on the rq's list. When the scheduler is freed, scx_sched_free_rcu_work() warns and frees the pcpu with the node still linked, and the list is walked again once the cpu comes back. An inactive cpu's local DSQ holds only tasks that are bound to it or are being moved off, so the reenq is pointless. Ignore reenqs of an inactive cpu's local DSQ. The test is lockless. The hotplug thread of a cpu going down runs on that cpu, and it marks the cpu inactive before it installs balance push. A dispatch on the cpu runs to completion before that thread can run there, so a dispatch that saw the cpu active has queued its callback by then. Requests from outside dispatch run from the wakeup path or through irq_work, which balance push doesn't affect. The grace period after the cpu goes inactive waits for any requester that saw it active, so that irq_work is queued while the cpu is online.

t: RDMA/uverbs: Fix DMABUF use-after-free during ufile cleanup
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: RDMA/uverbs: Fix DMABUF use-after-free during ufile cleanup The DMABUF release can race with ufile cleanup. When the cleanup holds hw_destroy_rwsem for write, uverbs_uobject_release() fails its trylock and leaves the uobject on the ufile list, but the dma_buf is freed as soon as the release returns. The cleanup then destroys the uobject and uses the freed dma_buf: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in uverbs_dmabuf_fd_destroy_uobj+0x46/0x200 Read of size 8 at addr ff11000109cf14b0 by task repro/435 Call Trace: uverbs_dmabuf_fd_destroy_uobj+0x46/0x200 destroy_hw_fd_uobject+0x3f/0x50 uverbs_destroy_uobject+0xc5/0x380 __uverbs_cleanup_ufile+0x1a8/0x260 uverbs_destroy_ufile_hw+0x54/0x160 ib_uverbs_close+0x34/0x110 Allocated by task 435: dma_buf_export+0x1b5/0x530 ib_uverbs_handler_UVERBS_METHOD_DMABUF_ALLOC+0x223/0x3f0 Freed by task 436: kfree+0x301/0x530 dentry_kill+0x14c/0x560 __fput+0x23a/0x4a0 rdma_user_mmap_entry_remove() dereferences the same pointer. Protect the stored dma_buf pointer with a mutex and clear it before release returns. Use a shared revoke helper so uobject destruction and mmap entry removal both skip a cleared pointer. Hold a temporary uobject reference across uverbs_uobject_release() and the pointer update. Use a separate mutex because uobject destruction can free the mmap entry before release finishes. Map and unmap use attachment->dmabuf directly, so they do not need to take the new mutex while holding the reservation lock.

t: RDMA/irdma: avoid use-after-free in icrdma_remove
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: RDMA/irdma: avoid use-after-free in icrdma_remove icrdma_remove() dereferences iwdev after calling irdma_ib_unregister_device(): irdma_ib_unregister_device(iwdev) -> ib_unregister_device(&iwdev->ibdev) -> __ib_unregister_device() -> ib_dealloc_device() irdma registers irdma_ib_dealloc_device() as the dealloc_driver callback in its ib_device_ops. The RDMA core explicitly documents ib_unregister_device() that when ops.dealloc_driver is used, ib_dev will be freed upon return from the function. The ib_device is embedded in struct irdma_device and iwdev itself was allocated by ib_alloc_device(irdma_device, ibdev). Consequently, once irdma_ib_unregister_device() returns, iwdev must no longer be dereferenced. However, icrdma_remove() currently accesses iwdev->rf afterwards when deinitializing interrupts, destroying ah_tbl_lock, and freeing rf. Although the final ib_device storage is released with kfree_rcu(), the object lifetime has already ended and callers must not rely on the RCU grace period to continue dereferencing iwdev. Save iwdev->rf before unregistering the RDMA device and use the saved pointer for the remaining cleanup. This issue was found by manual code inspection.

t: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body
d: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body. PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: rapidio: mport_cdev: fix use-after-free in mport_mm_close()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rapidio: mport_cdev: fix use-after-free in mport_mm_close() A use-after-free vulnerability was identified in mport_mm_close() in drivers/rapidio/devices/rio_mport_cdev.c, identical to the pattern previously addressed in dma_req_free(). This is observable from userspace when an application creates an mmap mapping via the RapidIO character device and subsequently unmaps it (or terminates, triggering exit_mmap()). During munmap, mport_mm_close() is invoked and drops the mapping reference via kref_put(). If kref_put() drops the last reference, mport_release_mapping() is called, which frees the underlying rio_mport_mapping structure. The subsequent mutex_unlock() then dereferences map->md to unlock buf_mutex, leading to a use-after-free: mport_mm_close() -> mutex_lock(&map->md->buf_mutex); ... -> kref_put(&map->ref, mport_release_mapping); /* map is freed */ -> mutex_unlock(&map->md->buf_mutex); /* UAF: map used */ Fix this by caching map->md before kref_put() and using the cached pointer for mutex unlocking, ensuring that freed memory is not accessed.

t: pps: generators: fix use-after-free when closing a removed device
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: pps: generators: fix use-after-free when closing a removed device The cdev of a PPS generator is embedded in struct pps_gen_device, but nothing ties the lifetime of that structure to the cdev: pps_gen is freed by the release function of its device, and an open file holds a device reference only until pps_gen_cdev_release() drops it. When the generator is unregistered while /dev/pps-genN is open, that put_device() drops the last reference and frees pps_gen, and __fput() then calls cdev_put() on the freed cdev: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in cdev_put+0x53/0x60 Read of size 8 at addr ffff88801383e138 by task ppsgen64/149 Call Trace: cdev_put+0x53/0x60 __fput+0x745/0xad0 fput_close_sync+0xd9/0x1b0 __x64_sys_close+0x86/0xf0 ... Freed by task 149: kfree+0x25a/0x6d0 device_release+0xca/0x3c0 kobject_put+0x169/0x320 pps_gen_cdev_release+0x51/0x80 __fput+0x36a/0xad0 pps.c had the same bug, fixed in commit c79a39dc8d06 ("pps: Fix a use-after-free"). Fix it the usual way: embed the struct device in pps_gen_device and register both with cdev_device_add(). This makes the device the parent of the cdev, so the cdev holds a device reference until the last file is closed.

t: PM: EM: Fix use-after-free of perf domain in netlink doit handlers
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: PM: EM: Fix use-after-free of perf domain in netlink doit handlers The doit handlers dropped em_pd_list_mutex before dereferencing the perf domain, so a concurrent device unregister could free it while the reply was being built. Encode the reply from em_perf_domain_for_id() callbacks, which run under the mutex, and allocate the skb outside of it, like the dumpit path already does. This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

t: platform/x86: asus-wmi: fix use-after-free unregistering kbd_led led
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: platform/x86: asus-wmi: fix use-after-free unregistering kbd_led led kbd_led_update_all() registers asus->kbd_led with devm_led_classdev_register() on the platform device, but kbd_led is embedded in struct asus_wmi, which asus_wmi_remove() frees at its end. The driver core calls .remove() before devres_release_all(), so the deferred devres release runs led_classdev_unregister() on memory that has already been freed. Whether that faults depends on whether the slab has been reused in between, which makes the crash on module unload intermittent and silently corrupts the led classdev state in the remaining runs. Unregister the led classdev explicitly in asus_wmi_led_exit(), after the led workqueue has been destroyed: kbd_led_work can then neither run nor be queued anymore, since asus_ref.asus is NULL too, so kbd_led_registered is stable and the classdev can be released while the memory embedding it is still alive. devm_led_classdev_unregister() also drops the devres entry, leaving nothing to run at unbind cleanup time; it warns when no devres entry exists, hence the kbd_led_registered check.

t: SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions
d: SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions. The SOAP extension reads an uninitialized array position when decoding an encoded array whose arraySize attribute is empty, whitespace-only or non-numeric, or when such dimensions come from a WSDL definition. Four bytes of unrelated heap data can then be used as an integer key in the decoded array. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a crafted request to a SoapServer endpoint, and a malicious SOAP server with a response to SoapClient. Heap memory is disclosed only if the application returns or otherwise exposes the decoded array. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: nvmet: fix use-after-free of the old registrant in nvmet_pr_preempt()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: fix use-after-free of the old registrant in nvmet_pr_preempt() nvmet_pr_preempt() handles a preempt sent by the reservation holder by changing the reservation type with nvmet_pr_update_reg_attr(), unless the reservation is of an All Registrants type. For the holder that helper does not modify the registrant in place: it puts a copy on the registrant list, points pr->holder to the copy and passes the old registrant to kfree_rcu(). If the reservation type changed, nvmet_pr_preempt() then hands &reg->hostid of that old registrant to nvmet_pr_resv_released(). Unless the reservation released notification is masked, that function takes subsys->lock and compares the host id against every controller of the subsystem. The caller only holds pr->pr_sem and is not in an RCU read-side critical section, so nothing keeps the old registrant alive while it is read. The result is a read of 16 freed bytes that decides which controllers get the notification. Found by code inspection. kfree_rcu() defers the free, so it usually happens after the read; when the pending free is forced to run before the read, KASAN reports the host id as freed memory. Pass the host id of the controller that sent the command instead. The registrant was looked up by that host id, and the controller outlives the request.

t: nvmet-fc: fix use-after-free in nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet-fc: fix use-after-free in nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection() nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection() looks up the association with nvmet_fc_find_target_assoc(), which returns it with a reference held, and drops that reference as soon as the target queue has been allocated. iod->assoc is then dereferenced again by nvmet_fc_makeconnid() while building the connection id. The queue only borrows the pointer and takes no reference of its own. Once the lookup reference is dropped the association is kept alive solely by the reference taken when it was created, so a disconnect LS or a remote port unregister running concurrently can free it before nvmet_fc_makeconnid() reads it: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work (drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:193 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1841 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1995 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:2021) Read of size 8 at addr ffff888179f1b000 by task kworker/u9:2/1167 Hardware name: QEMU Ubuntu 24.04 PC v2 (i440FX + PIIX, arch_caps fix, 1996), BIOS 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2 04/01/2014 Workqueue: nvmet-wq nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work Call Trace: <TASK> dump_stack_lvl (lib/dump_stack.c:94 lib/dump_stack.c:120) print_report (mm/kasan/report.c:378 mm/kasan/report.c:482) kasan_report (mm/kasan/report.c:595) nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work (drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:193 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1841 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1995 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:2021) process_scheduled_works (kernel/workqueue.c:3322 kernel/workqueue.c:3405) worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3486) kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436) ret_from_fork (archkernel/process.c:158) ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245) </TASK> Freed by task 1167 on cpu 0 at 405.998150s: kasan_save_track (mm/kasan/common.c:57 mm/kasan/common.c:78) kasan_save_free_info (mm/kasan/generic.c:584) __kasan_slab_free (mm/kasan/common.c:253 mm/kasan/common.c:285) kfree (include/linux/kasan.h:235 mm/slub.c:2705 mm/slub.c:6405 mm/slub.c:6720) nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work (drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1808 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1995 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:2021) process_scheduled_works (kernel/workqueue.c:3322 kernel/workqueue.c:3405) object at ffff888179f1b000 which belongs to the cache kmalloc-2k of size 2048 The buggy address is located 0 bytes inside of freed 2048-byte region [ffff888179f1b000, ffff888179f1b800) Hold the lookup reference until the response has been built, and drop it on the error path as well.

t: iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free iommufd_eventq_fops_release() drops the file's users reference before reading eventq->ictx. Once that reference is dropped, IOMMU_DESTROY in another thread can remove and free the event queue, so the later load accesses freed memory. Read ictx while the users reference still pins the event queue, then drop the reference and put the saved context. The context reference taken by iommufd_eventq_init() keeps ictx valid until the put. Fault and vEVENTQ file descriptors share this release path.

t: Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers
d: Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers. The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service. This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: landlock: Fix superblock use-after-free in release_inode()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: landlock: Fix superblock use-after-free in release_inode() Without this fix, release_inode() (task 1) can race with a umount operation in hook_sb_delete() (task 2). The order of operations in which the race occurs is: * task 2: hook_sb_delete() arrives at the end of the function, waiting for landlock_superblock(sb)->inode_refs to become zero. * task 1: release_inode(): does atomic_long_dec_and_test(), decrementing inode_refs to zero. * task 2: gets woken up through some other means, sees that inode_refs is zero and returns. The caller is the unmount operation and proceeds to release the superblock. * task 1: Runs wake_up_var(&landlock_superblock(sb)->inode_refs), *dereferencing the sb_security on the freed-up superblock*. Notably, wake_up_var() does not dereference the pointer passed to it, and only uses it to determine an overapproximated set of tasks to wake up. So while it's potentially possible for an attacker to provide a different value for that pointer, this only results in the wrong set of tasks getting woken up, and in this scenario, no further tasks are actually waiting. Nevertheless, KASAN detects it as a slab-use-after-free read on sb->s_security: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in release_inode+0x196/0x290 Read of size 8 at addr ffff888103b6c0a8 by task repro/217 release_inode+0x196/0x290 landlock_put_object+0x71/0x90 landlock_free_rules+0x38/0xc0 landlock_put_ruleset+0x47/0x130 fop_ruleset_release+0x33/0x40 __fput+0x305/0x780 Freed by task 54: kfree+0x11c/0x390 process_scheduled_works+0x766/0xe50 worker_thread+0x7bc/0xb20 The fix is to determine &landlock_superblock(inode->i_sb)->inode_refs only once earlier in release_inode(), and later use that precalculated address for the wake_up_var() call, without having to dereference through the superblock.

t: lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). The nlm_blocked list reference is all that keeps the block alive across that window. nlmsvc_grant_blocked() does take one of its own, but not until after the lock has been dropped. Unmounting the nfsd filesystem while a lock request is still blocked reaches nlmsvc_traverse_blocks(), which drops the list reference and frees the block along with the nlm_rqst hanging off it. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230 Read of size 8 at addr ffff88811b04c808 by task lockd/8377 nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230 nlmsvc_retry_blocked+0x61c/0x800 lockd+0x144/0x1c0 Freed by task 8392: nlmsvc_release_block+0x231/0x290 nlmsvc_traverse_blocks+0x139/0x1b0 nlm_traverse_files+0x1aa/0xa00 nlmsvc_free_host_resources+0x12/0x60 nlm_shutdown_hosts_net+0x127/0x280 lockd_down+0xd5/0x1c0 Take a reference before releasing nlm_blocked_lock and drop it once the retry has run.

t: media: au0828: fix use-after-free in bulk_timeout timer on disconnect
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: au0828: fix use-after-free in bulk_timeout timer on disconnect start_urb_transfer() arms dev->bulk_timeout, whose callback au0828_bulk_timeout() queues dev->restart_streaming; that work in turn calls start_urb_transfer() and re-arms the timer. au0828_dvb_unregister() cancels restart_streaming on disconnect but does not sync bulk_timeout. au0828_usb_release() then frees dev with kfree(), so a timer still armed or pending at that point can fire after the free and dereference dev through timer_container_of(). Sync the timer with timer_shutdown_sync() before cancel_work_sync(). The timer callback queues the work, so the timer must be stopped first; the shutdown variant is needed because the work re-arms the timer through start_urb_transfer(). The dvb->frontend == NULL early return guards the register-failure path where the timer was never set up. This bug was found by static analysis.

t: Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input
d: Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input. The Uri\Rfc3986\Uri class does not correctly handle the output-size limit and errors of the uriparser library when converting a URI back to a string. For a URI whose string representation reaches approximately 2 GiB, toString(), toRawString() and other serializing operations can return a truncated or invalid string instead of an error. An application that accepts attacker-controlled URI data of that size, has enough memory to process it and trusts the result may make incorrect validation or routing decisions, and the large allocations can exhaust memory. parse_url() and Uri\WhatWg\Url are not affected. This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: media: cx23885: Fix use-after-free in cx23885_finidev due to race condition
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: cx23885: Fix use-after-free in cx23885_finidev due to race condition In cx23885_v4l2_dev_notify_init, &dev->cx25840_work is bound with cx23885_av_work_handler, and &dev->ir_rx_work and &dev->ir_tx_work are bound with cx23885_ir_rx_work_handler and cx23885_ir_tx_work_handler. cx23885_irq can schedule these works on system_wq when an AV_CORE interrupt is received, and the IR subdevice can also schedule the IR works from its interrupt service routine via the v4l2_device notify callback. If we remove the device, cx23885_finidev makes cleanup and the memory allocated for dev is released by kfree(dev), while the works mentioned above may still be pending or running. The sequence of operations that may lead to a UAF bug is as follows: CPU0 CPU1 | cx23885_irq | schedule_work(&dev->cx25840_work) cx23885_finidev | cx23885_input_fini(dev) | cx23885_ir_fini(dev) | cx23885_shutdown(dev) | free_irq(pci_dev->irq, dev) | pci_disable_device(pci_dev) | cx23885_dev_unregister(dev) | v4l2_device_unregister(v4l2_dev) | kfree(dev) | // dev is freed | | cx23885_av_work_handler | // use dev (use-after-free) Fix it by canceling the works after the IRQ handler that can schedule them has been stopped, and before proceeding with the remaining cleanup in cx23885_finidev. Note that the flush_work() calls in cx23885_input_ir_stop() do not close this race: they only wait for works that are already queued or running at that moment, they do not prevent the IRQ handler, which is still registered at that point, from scheduling the works again afterwards, and they are skipped entirely when dev->sd_ir is NULL. The cancel_work_sync() calls are therefore placed after free_irq(), the only point at which no new work can be scheduled.

t: media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path hackrf_alloc_urbs() frees the URBs it allocated so far when one allocation fails, but leaves the entries in dev->urb_list[] and dev->urbs_initialized untouched. The caller, hackrf_start_streaming(), then calls hackrf_free_urbs() on the error path, which walks dev->urbs_initialized entries and calls usb_free_urb() a second time on the already-freed URBs, causing a use-after-free (slab-use-after-free Write in usb_free_urb()). Drop the redundant cleanup loop inside hackrf_alloc_urbs() and let hackrf_free_urbs(), which the caller already invokes on error, own the cleanup of the successfully allocated URBs.

t: media: imon: fix use-after-free in display_close via dev_dbg
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: imon: fix use-after-free in display_close via dev_dbg ictx->dev is a raw pointer to the usb_interface's embedded device. On disconnect, usb_disconnect() can drop the last reference on the interface and free it while a userspace fd for /dev/lcd0 is still open. When that fd is later closed, display_close() dereferences the now-freed ictx->dev via dev_dbg(), causing a use-after-free. Remove the dev_dbg() calls that dereference ictx->dev in display_close() and free_imon_context(), rather than taking a reference on the device.

t: media: ipu-bridge: Fix use-after-free in IVSC error path
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: ipu-bridge: Fix use-after-free in IVSC error path ipu_bridge_get_ivsc_acpi_dev() returns an ACPI device with a reference held. If no matching CSI device is found, ipu_bridge_check_ivsc_dev() drops that reference before passing the device to dev_err(). Concurrent CSI device and ACPI namespace removal can drop the other references, making this the final put. dev_err() then reads the freed struct acpi_device and its kobject name. This was reproduced without kprobes by racing normal CSI platform-device unregistration and ACPI configfs table removal against the production ipu_bridge_init() entry. KASAN reported the final free through device_release(), followed by invalid reads through _dev_err(). Emit the error message while the lookup reference is still held, then drop the reference as before. Source reproducers and vulnerable/fixed serial logs, with only the build hostname redacted, are available at: https://github.com/kimaiden1984-boop/linux-ipu-bridge-acpi-uaf-reproducer The fixed target builds with W=1 on x86-64. This was not tested on physical IPU hardware. The tests establish runtime reachability but do not measure occurrence frequency on shipping systems or establish exploitability.

t: mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free in hugetlb_mfill_atomic_pte()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free in hugetlb_mfill_atomic_pte() Let's fix another instance where we use a folio after dropping the PTL, where someone else could e.g., MADV_DONTNEED it once we drop the PTL, making us trigger a use-after-free on the folio.

t: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation
d: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation. When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images. This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio For a fault in a private mapping with nothing in the page cache, hugetlb_no_page() allocates a folio, locks it and maps it. The folio has one reference, which belongs to the page table entry from then on. After dropping the page table lock the function still sets the migratable flag of the folio and unlocks it. Whoever zaps the entry in between frees the folio. The fault holds the fault mutex and the lock of the vma. MADV_DONTNEED and the first unmap of a hole punch, hugetlb_vmdelete_list(), do not take the fault mutex, and a private vma only has a lock if it owns a reservation map: not with MAP_NORESERVE, and not in the child after fork(). Then the flag is set in, and folio_unlock() is called on, a folio that is free or has a new owner. A surplus page goes back to the page allocator while it is locked: BUG: Bad page state in process init pfn:108e00 flags: 0x200000000000059(locked|uptodate|dirty|head|node=0|zone=2) page dumped because: PAGE_FLAGS_CHECK_AT_FREE flag(s) set A page of the pool can be given to the next user, of any file, who locks it and loses the lock to the late folio_unlock(): kernel BUG at mm/filemap.c:1532! hugetlb_no_page+0x111b/0x23e0 hugetlb_fault+0x3a9/0x14a0 An unprivileged process is enough: threads that write to a MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_NORESERVE hugetlb mapping, threads that call MADV_DONTNEED on it, and one that takes the freed pages for another file. Until commit 3a47c54f09c4 ("hugetlbfs: revert use i_mmap_rwsem for more pmd sharing synchronization") the fault held i_mmap_rwsem for reading, which everybody who zaps takes for writing. The lock that commit bf4916922c60 ("hugetlbfs: extend hugetlb_vma_lock to private VMAs") gave to private vmas closed the window again, but only for those with a reservation map. Be done with the folio before the page table lock is dropped, as hugetlb_wp() is with its copy. The function already unlocks page cache folios under that lock. Original fix generated by an LLM and sent in private by Josef. [david@kernel.org: simplify+move comment]

t: apparmor: fix a use-after-free in aa_lookupn_ns()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: apparmor: fix a use-after-free in aa_lookupn_ns() aa_lookupn_ns() takes a reference on the namespace it finds with aa_get_ns(), which is kref_get() on the reference count that the namespace is released through, without checking whether the namespace is still in use. A concurrent removal of a ":"-prefixed namespace looks the same namespace up and only then takes the parent lock to remove it, so the last reference can be dropped between the lookup and the aa_get_ns() call: the reference count then reports the increment on a zero count and the kernel classifies the following use of the object as a use-after-free. A user with CAP_MAC_ADMIN can trigger this by writing a ":<name>" removal and a ":<name>/<profile>" removal to /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/.remove concurrently. refcount_t: addition on 0; use-after-free. WARNING: lib/refcount.c:25 at refcount_warn_saturate+0xc0/0xe0, CPU#6 Call Trace: <TASK> aa_lookupn_ns+0xa9/0xc0 aa_remove_profiles+0x4fb/0x730 ? __kvmalloc_node_noprof+0x219/0x5c0 ? __pfx_aa_remove_profiles+0x10/0x10 ? aa_loaddata_alloc+0x65/0x1f0 ? _copy_from_user+0x2d/0x80 ? aa_loaddata_alloc+0x111/0x1f0 profile_remove+0x2ee/0x4a0 vfs_write+0x21e/0xcf0 ? rcu_core+0x29c/0x1740 ? timerqueue_linked_add+0x1f4/0x3d0 ? __pfx_vfs_write+0x10/0x10 ? mutex_lock+0x81/0xe0 ? __pfx_mutex_lock+0x10/0x10 ? __pfx_rcu_core+0x10/0x10 ? __pfx_hrtimer_update_next_event+0x10/0x10 ? mutex_unlock+0x7b/0xd0 ? fdget_pos+0x24d/0x4b0 ksys_write+0xf7/0x1c0 ? __pfx_ksys_write+0x10/0x10 ? restore_fpregs_from_fpstate+0x37/0xc0 do_syscall_64+0xf9/0x540 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK> Fix by rejecting a namespace whose reference count is zero.

t: ASoC: audio-graph-card2: Fix use-after-free in audio_graph2_link_c2c()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ASoC: audio-graph-card2: Fix use-after-free in audio_graph2_link_c2c() of_graph_get_next_port() consumes the reference of its prev argument. port0 is only borrowed from the caller's iterator, so the call drops a reference the function does not own, and port0 is dereferenced again afterwards. Pass an extra reference, as graph_count_c2c() does, so the reference the callee consumes is the one taken here.

t: ata: sata_fsl: Fix use-after-free of host_priv on probe() failure
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ata: sata_fsl: Fix use-after-free of host_priv on probe() failure sata_fsl_host_stop() releases hcr_base and host_priv: static void sata_fsl_host_stop(struct ata_host *host) { struct sata_fsl_host_priv *host_priv = host->private_data; iounmap(host_priv->hcr_base); kfree(host_priv); } ->host_stop() is called by the driver core through the ata_host_stop() devres action which ata_host_start() registers, so it is called both when the device is unbound and when probe() fails after the host has been started. The error_exit_with_cleanup label of sata_fsl_probe() releases hcr_base and host_priv as well, and it is reachable from the two device_create_file() calls which are done after the host has been activated. In that case sata_fsl_host_stop() runs on an already freed host_priv, resulting in a use-after-free and a double iounmap()/kfree(). Add a separate error label for the failures happening after the host has been activated, which only detaches the host and leaves hcr_base and host_priv to sata_fsl_host_stop(). Note that ata_host_detach() is dropped from error_exit_with_cleanup, as that label is now only reachable while host is still NULL.

t: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution
d: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution. In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

t: s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup zpci_remove_parent_msi_domain() dereferences zbus->msi_parent_domain unconditionally and does not clear it afterwards. zpci_bus_create_pci_bus() removes the domain when pci_create_root_bus() fails, then zpci_bus_release() removes it again on the last kref_put(), reading ->fwnode from the freed irq_domain and freeing it twice. If zpci_alloc_domain() or zpci_create_parent_msi_domain() fails, no domain is created at all; zbus is kzalloc'd, so the same release path dereferences NULL. Return early when there is no domain, and clear the pointer after removing one.

t: s390/pci: Fix MSI directed-mode teardown IRQ bit count
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: s390/pci: Fix MSI directed-mode teardown IRQ bit count On s390 with directed interrupts enabled, zpci_msi_teardown_directed() frees the platform's maximum number of MSI bits (zdev->max_msi) instead of the actual allocated count (zdev->msi_nr_irqs). This corrupts the shared IRQ bitmap used by all PCI functions, causing lost interrupts and heap corruption. Fix zpci_msi_teardown_directed() to only free the actual allocated IRQ bit count.

t: s390/pci: Fix resource leak in zpci MSI setup
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: s390/pci: Fix resource leak in zpci MSI setup If airq_iv_create() fails in __alloc_airq(), the zpci_sbv bit allocated by airq_iv_alloc_bit() is never freed. This permanently leaks one of the ZPCI_NR_DEVICES summary bits, reducing system capacity with each failed device hotplug. In systems with repeated device insertion failures or under memory pressure, all summary bits can be exhausted, preventing new PCI devices from being added until reboot.
